name: IN JI
title: Backend Engineer

skill_groups.name: Infrastructure
items: AWS (EC2, ECS, RDS, S3, ECR, Route53, Lambda, SQS, Secrets Manager, CloudFront)

intro: **I enjoy simplifying repetitive work and improving the systems behind running services.** When building a feature, I consider how people will use it and what it will take to operate it day to day.

When operations staff had to ask developers or connect to servers for routine tasks, I built internal web tools they could use themselves. I enjoyed **changing how work gets done through software**, and began looking for ways to remove manual steps elsewhere.

Expanding services across countries and migrating APIs taught me to check how code changes affect existing features and operations. I am interested in **changing system structures while keeping services running**.

With re:feel, an app I co-planned with a friend, I also built and operated a product myself. I developed the app and backend, handled deployment, and used usage data and feedback to refine its target audience and features after launch. I enjoy seeing how people use a product and turning their responses into the next improvement.

I use MCP to review product specifications alongside related code and work with AI on implementation plans and repetitive tasks. I verify generated code myself and choose architectures and technologies based on service requirements and operating conditions.

companies.name: smaxh
companies.description: Tennis matching, lessons, and community platform. Backend development and operations for services in Korea, the US, and Australia.
highlights: **Python · Django · MySQL backend for match and lesson payments and settlement** — Built payment, cancellation, refund, and withdrawal flows. Supported a service whose monthly payment volume grew from **KRW 200M to 400M**, and transaction count from **16K to 30K**, between August and October 2025.

**Docker · Terraform · AWS integration of COOCON balance withdrawals** — Built the infrastructure and APIs to withdraw SMAXH Pay balances to bank accounts. Configured Docker, Terraform, S3 environment settings, and Secrets Manager credentials; developed account registration, lookup, withdrawal, and transaction history APIs and deployed the application.
**No-show deposit payments, refunds, and settlement** — Contributed to the full deposit-processing flow; the deposit configuration rate was **78% in September 2026**.

**Web authentication compatible with the existing app** — Integrated Google, Apple, and Kakao web login with existing signup and account-linking flows. Separated app and web sessions and configured environment-specific deployment settings while preserving app compatibility.

**DynamoDB-based global account integration** — Kept country-specific databases separate while linking accounts through shared UUIDs. Added shared-state validation to login and token refresh to resolve cross-country inconsistencies in account closure and re-registration.

**US and Australian launch validation** — Integrated local tennis-court data and found incorrect match dates caused by server and court time-zone differences during pre-launch testing. Changed scheduling to use court-local time, verified the fixes, and deployed before launch.

**Shared APIs for social and tier-based matches** — Consolidated response and processing structures and reused payment and notification logic. Retained legacy endpoints so the existing app could coexist with the new APIs.

**pytest · Docker test environments and regression tests** — Set up MySQL and DynamoDB Local to test payment, refund, settlement, authentication, and account-linking APIs. Wrote success and failure tests, including duplicate processing and concurrent session refresh and revocation.

**Lesson development and operational query optimization** — Built recurring-schedule, application, payment, and settlement models and APIs. Used Datadog APM and SQL to diagnose bottlenecks and reduce repeated lookups, unnecessary joins, and aggregation work.

companies.name: Playtag
companies.description: AI video analysis of preschool children's behavior. Built internal web applications for analysis reruns and client configuration.
highlights: **Python web application for rerunning failed video-analysis jobs** — Built and deployed an internal web application where staff could select targets and request reruns. Replaced server access and manual code execution, reducing preparation time from **about 1 hour to 5 minutes or less**.

**Self-service client configuration for operations staff** — Enabled operations staff to record and apply kindergarten schedules and settings directly, reducing developer handoffs and manual code changes. Deployed on a low-cost single instance suited to internal usage.
**Kotlin · Spring Boot APIs for kindergarten student management** — Built the complete set of new APIs **within a one-week sprint**, applying both technologies in production for the first time.

companies.name: Artue.io
companies.description: Art commerce and online exhibition platform. Worked on media processing, AWS infrastructure, and API migration for a running service.
highlights: **Python · Serverless Framework · S3/Lambda asynchronous media processing** — Reduced the loading burden of high-resolution originals by generating WebP images and multiple video resolutions after upload. Used in-memory streams instead of temporary files and excluded derived-file events to prevent duplicate conversions.

**Terraform · AWS EC2/ECS infrastructure and Auto Scaling configuration** — Changed instances from **t3.medium to t3.small** and the CPU scaling target from **40% to 20%**, consolidating environment-specific capacity settings.

**Gradual API and TypeORM migration** — Migrated customer, artwork, and purchasing functionality while **running v2 and v3 APIs in parallel**. Added validation tests so the frontend could adopt new APIs one feature at a time.

**Multi-currency purchasing and payments** — Applied exchange rates, discounts, and shipping costs across carts, orders, and payments for currencies including EUR and THB. Integrated Naver Pay, supported its approval process, and restored coupons on cancellation.

companies.name: Viewee Inc.
companies.description: Services connecting user-contributed data, AI analysis, and blockchain rewards. Developed data validation automation and transaction APIs.
highlights: **Python · Airflow automation of image-annotation review** — Applied bounding-box and OCR cross-checks and text-similarity validation to labels previously reviewed by hand, and automated recurring checks.
**TypeScript · NestJS APIs for EarnTube token transactions** — Built history models to track transaction results and hashes, and migrated legacy points history.

companies.name: re:feel
companies.description: AI journaling app offering diary analysis and illustrations. Co-planned with a friend; personally developed and deployed the app and backend.
highlights: **Django/DRF · MySQL · React/Capacitor AI journaling app** — Co-planned the product with a friend, built the app and backend myself, and handled AWS deployment. **Launched on iOS and Android in about two months**.

**AI analysis and in-app purchase integration** — Connected asynchronous Gemini analysis and illustration results, translation, server-side purchase validation, and access entitlements to the app experience.

**Firebase data and user feedback for product improvements** — Shifted focus to Korean users and combined feature improvements with social media promotion; **cumulative signups grew from about 10 to over 100 within weeks**.
